agenda: Identical letters dated 19 January 2016 from the Permanent Representative of Colombia to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General and the President of the Security Council (S/2016/53); Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (S/2025/595)
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The UK's primary objective is to maintain Council consensus (15-0-0) to grant a full one-year renewal for the UN Verification Mission in Colombia while safeguarding the primacy of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and its key provisions on rural reform, ethnic communities, transitional justice (SJP), and Women, Peace and Security. The most contentious negotiations will likely centre on calibrating language regarding the Government's ongoing "Total Peace" dialogues and potential ceasefire monitoring mandates involving disparate armed groups (such as the ELN and EMC factions), where Council members hold differing views regarding mission overstretch versus supporting broader peace initiatives.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Reaffirming its full commitment to the peace process in the Republic of Colombia,

Recalling all its resolutions and Presidential and press statements regarding the peace process in Colombia,

Welcoming the progress made towards peace across Colombia since the adoption of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement for Ending the Conflict and Building a Stable and Lasting Peace (the Final Agreement), urging the parties, with the support of relevant state institutions and security forces, as well as civil society including women and youth, to work together to continue building upon this progress and address ongoing challenges, in particular the continued violence in conflict-affected areas, through comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement, including rural reform, inclusive political participation, its ethnic and gender provisions, and countering illicit drugs including through crop substitution programmes, and recalling the disproportionate impact of the conflict on women and its effects on persons belonging to Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities as well as children,

Taking note of the engagement of the Peacebuilding Commission with the Government of Colombia and the Security Council, particularly on rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter and Transitional Justice, and looking forward to further cooperation, including with the relevant United Nations agencies, funds and programmes in order to ensure an integrated and coherent approach to the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement,

Recalling in particular its resolution 2366 (2017) which established the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (the Verification Mission) to verify implementation by the Government of Colombia and Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC-EP) of sections 3.2 and 3.4 of the Final Agreement as called for in section 6.3.3 of the Final Agreement, and recalling the positive role played by the Verification Mission in that regard, in verifying the implementation of reintegration efforts and comprehensive security guarantees for former combatants and communities, and emphasizing the efforts of the Verification Mission to continue to integrate a gender perspective as a cross-cutting issue into its planning, verification and reporting, recognizing the importance of other perspectives including development, ensuring adequate gender expertise as appropriate, and continuing support, within its current mandate, for victims and survivors of conflict, including from sexual and gender-based violence, in particular their referral to safe and accessible assistance provided by the relevant Colombian authorities,

Recalling also its resolution 2574 (2021) which expanded the mandate of the Verification Mission to include the additional task of verifying compliance with and implementation of the sentences to be issued by the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (SJP), and welcoming the ongoing preparations and cooperation between the Verification Mission and the SJP in this regard,

Noting that, under the terms of the Final Agreement, the sentences of the SJP will have the overall aim of realizing the rights of victims and consolidating peace, and will need to have the greatest restorative and reparative function in relation to the harm caused,

Recognizing the contribution the Verification Mission makes to building confidence in the Comprehensive System for Truth, Justice, Reparation and Non-Repetition established under the Final Agreement, which is integral to the success of the peace process and the fulfilment of the rights of the victims of the conflict,

Recalling its resolution 2673 (2023) which expanded the mandate of the Verification Mission to include the additional task of monitoring the implementation of section 1 on comprehensive rural reform and section 6.2 on the Ethnic Chapter of the Final Agreement, emphasizing the crucial role of implementing comprehensive rural reform, including issues of land access and rural development, in tackling structural factors underlying the conflict, and underlining the importance of the implementation of the Ethnic Chapter, which is a critical aspect of the Final Agreement,

Recalling also its resolution 2694 (2023) which expanded the mandate of the Verification Mission, and reaffirming the authorization of the additional deployments in resolution 2694 (2023) to facilitate the effective implementation of its mandate,

Expressing its hope for renewed progress in dialogue between the Government of Colombia and armed groups to achieve sustainable ceasefires and reduce violence against civilian populations, and recalling the Secretary-General’s proposal to keep the Council abreast of developments, including conflict dynamics at local levels between armed groups,

Reiterating its willingness to consider mandating the Verification Mission to monitor and verify the implementation of ceasefire agreements between the Government of Colombia and armed groups when the Secretary-General confirms that appropriate conditions, including verifiable protocols and mutual commitment by the parties, have been reached,

Recalling the importance of continued implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, as set out in resolution 2307 (2016), welcoming the Government of Colombia’s efforts to seek broader peace through dialogue, stressing the importance of strengthening the State’s presence across conflict-affected regions for transforming the territories, and recognizing that ceasefire agreements are a step towards the development of more comprehensive peace agreements,

Underlining in this regard the primary importance of the Verification Mission in supporting the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, acknowledging the role of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General in supporting political peace dialogues to date, and stressing the need to keep the Council abreast of these activities,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of the Verification Mission until 31 October 2026;

2. Expresses its willingness to work with the Government of Colombia on the further extension of the mandate of the Verification Mission on the basis of agreement between the parties.

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We welcome the balanced text, which appropriately reaffirms support for the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, particularly its rural reform and ethnic provisions, while respecting Colombia's national ownership and sovereignty. We commend the penholder's efforts and are ready to support the adoption of the resolution as drafted.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for a period of one year. We commend the Colombian Government's sustained efforts to advance the peace process, particularly through rural reform and peaceful dialogue to address the root causes of conflict. We appreciate the penholder's balanced text and look forward to the Council maintaining its unity on this agenda item.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom extending the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We commend the balanced text, which appropriately underscores the vital importance of the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, transitional justice through the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, and the central role of gender equality and the Ethnic Chapter. We look forward to the swift and unanimous adoption of this text.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom to renew the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We welcome the balanced text, which appropriately underscores the central importance of comprehensively implementing the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, including transitional justice, rural reform, and gender and ethnic provisions. France stands ready to co-sponsor the text and looks forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for an additional year. We commend the United Kingdom for circulating a balanced text that reflects the Council's sustained commitment to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. Greece attaches great importance to the work of the Verification Mission, particularly regarding transitional justice, security guarantees, rural reform, and the protection of vulnerable groups, and we look forward to the swift adoption of this text by consensus.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its full support for the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2026. We commend the United Kingdom for presenting a well-balanced text that preserves Council consensus and maintains vital focus on the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, particularly comprehensive rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, and transitional justice. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We commend the continued commitment of the Colombian Government and people to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and value the constructive role played by the Verification Mission. Pakistan appreciates the penholder's balanced text and looks forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2026. As an immediate neighbor, Panama recognizes that peace, stability, and the rule of law in Colombia are essential for regional security and prosperity. We commend the penholder for presenting a balanced text that reflects the Council's sustained commitment and consensus behind the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We commend the Mission's indispensable role in supporting the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, including through rural reform, transitional justice, and engagement with the Peacebuilding Commission. We look forward to the swift and unanimous adoption of this text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We commend the continued efforts of President Gustavo Petro's administration towards the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, particularly regarding rural reform and the Ethnic Chapter. We value the constructive role played by the Verification Mission and guarantor countries, and we are ready to support the adoption of the text as drafted.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone commends the United Kingdom for preparing a balanced draft resolution that ensures the continuity of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We fully support the extension of the mandate until 31 October 2026 and appreciate the continued focus on the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, and transitional justice mechanisms. We stand ready to support the swift adoption of the resolution by consensus.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom to extend the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We particularly appreciate the continued focus on the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, including the gender and ethnic provisions, transitional justice, and the crucial work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace. We are ready to support the timely adoption of the text as drafted.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2026. We commend the Government and people of Colombia for their continued commitment to the implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and their pursuit of broader peace through dialogue. Somalia welcomes the balanced text prepared by the United Kingdom and stands ready to support its adoption as circulated.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks the United Kingdom for circulating this well-balanced draft resolution extending the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We remain steadfast in our partnership with Colombia and fully support the Mission's critical work, particularly regarding the Ethnic Chapter, rural reform, and transitional justice through the Special Jurisdiction for Peace. We are ready to support the text as drafted and look forward to its unanimous adoption.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United Kingdom appreciates the unanimous support across the Council for the draft resolution extending the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2026. Because all delegations supported the draft text without proposing changes, the text is maintained as circulated. The draft resolution reflects unified Council backing for the Colombian peace process and is positioned for unanimous adoption.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria consistently supports the peace process in Colombia and the extension of the mandate of the UN Verification Mission, aligning with our prior voting record and consensus among Council members.
reasons.China: China consistently supports the Colombian peace process and the work of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia in assisting the parties to implement the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, aligning with the host government's consent and Council consensus. Following standard Council practice on this consensus file, China delivers its statement after the vote rather than before.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the Colombian peace process and the vital work of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia, aligning with the unanimous consensus across the Council to extend its mandate for another year.
reasons.France: France consistently and steadfastly supports the Colombian peace process and the UN Verification Mission, aligning with all Council members to renew the mandate unanimously, reserving its remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece fully supports the Colombian peace process and the essential work of the UN Verification Mission, aligning with Council consensus to extend the mandate for an additional year.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana strongly supports the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and the renewal of the Verification Mission's mandate in Colombia, and in line with standard Council practice on this consensus item, our delegation will vote in favour and deliver any remarks after the adoption.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the extension of the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia in line with the host country's consent and Council consensus.
reasons.Panama: Panama strongly supports the peace process in neighboring Colombia and the renewal of the mandate of the UN Verification Mission, aligning with full Council consensus.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea consistently supports the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and the renewal of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia's mandate, aligning with our prior voting record and consensus among all Council members.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia consistently supports the peace process in Colombia, the Colombian Government's peace efforts, and the renewal of the UN Verification Mission's mandate, which enjoys consensus across the Security Council and the consent of the host country.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia, particularly emphasizing the implementation of the Ethnic Chapter, rural reform, and transitional justice mechanisms.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia steadfastly supports the 2016 Final Peace Agreement in Colombia and the renewal of the UN Verification Mission's mandate, which enjoys consensus across the Council.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the peace process in Colombia and the extension of the mandate of the UN Verification Mission, aligning with the unanimous Council consensus and our position expressed during negotiations.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: As the penholder and author of the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia, the United Kingdom fully supports its adoption and will speak after the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the 2016 Final Peace Agreement in Colombia and the vital work of the UN Verification Mission, consistent with our long-standing policy, bilateral partnership with Colombia, and our voting record on this agenda item.

after.China:
China welcomes the Security Council’s unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. This once again demonstrates the Council’s united and firm support for the peace process in Colombia and the efforts of the Colombian Government and people to achieve lasting peace and stability.

The 2016 Final Peace Agreement is a historic milestone. Its comprehensive and sustained implementation is essential for consolidating peace gains and addressing the root causes of conflict. China appreciates the Colombian Government’s continued commitment to advancing the peace process, in particular its efforts in comprehensive rural reform, land access, and social and economic development in conflict-affected regions. We believe that development is the foundation of peace, and we hope the relevant development and reintegration plans will continue to deliver tangible dividends of peace to the Colombian people, especially former combatants and vulnerable communities.

China supports the Colombian Government’s pursuit of broader peace through dialogue and political negotiations, which has set an inspiring example of resolving conflict through peaceful means. We hope that all parties concerned will demonstrate political will, build mutual trust, reduce violence against civilians, and make sustained efforts towards lasting ceasefires and comprehensive peace.

China commends the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia and Special Representative Massieu for their tireless work. We hope that the Mission will continue to strictly implement its mandate, strengthen coordination and cooperation with the Colombian Government, respect Colombia’s sovereignty and ownership, and continue to manage its resources in an efficient and effective manner. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue playing a constructive role in supporting Colombia on its path towards comprehensive peace, stability, and prosperity.

Thank you.
after.Guyana:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the A3+ members, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone, Somalia, and my own country, Guyana.

The A3+ welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year, and we thank the United Kingdom, as penholder, for its efforts in facilitating a consensus text.

Today’s unanimous decision reaffirms the Council’s unwavering commitment to supporting the Government and people of Colombia in their pursuit of lasting and sustainable peace. As we approach the ninth anniversary of the signing of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, Colombia continues to demonstrate what can be achieved through dialogue, political will, and dedicated international support.

While commendable progress has been recorded, significant challenges remain, particularly persistent violence in conflict-affected regions. The A3+ remains deeply concerned by the continued threats and violence directed against former combatants, social leaders, human rights defenders, as well as the disproportionate impact of conflict on women, children, and persons belonging to Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities.

We reiterate our conviction that the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement remains the foundational cornerstone for peace. In this regard, we underscore the critical importance of accelerating the implementation of the Ethnic Chapter and Comprehensive Rural Reform, which are vital for addressing the historical and structural inequalities that fuel conflict. We also welcome the ongoing work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (SJP) and look forward to the Mission’s verification of the restorative sentences.

Furthermore, the A3+ continues to support the Colombian Government’s broader peace initiatives and dialogue with armed groups aimed at de-escalating violence, protecting civilians, and expanding state presence in underserved territories. 

In conclusion, the A3+ reaffirms its full support to the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Mr. Carlos Ruiz Massieu, and to all the women and men of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia for their tireless dedication in accompanying Colombia on its path towards comprehensive and durable peace.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for a further year. We would like to thank all Council members for their constructive engagement and continued united support throughout the negotiations.

Today’s consensus vote sends a clear and enduring message of the Security Council’s unwavering commitment to the peace process in Colombia. It reaffirms our strong partnership with the Colombian Government and its people, as well as our continued backing for the comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement as the foundation for lasting stability.

As we approach the ninth anniversary of the Final Agreement, sustained momentum is vital across all its chapters, including comprehensive rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, and the crucial work of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace as it advances towards issuing its first restorative sentences. We also underline the critical need to address continued violence in conflict-affected regions, to protect social leaders, human rights defenders, and former combatants, and to safeguard indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities.

Following the conclusion of the annual high-level open debate on women and peace and security earlier this week, the United Kingdom is especially pleased that this resolution continues to recognize the importance of integrating a gender perspective across all aspects of the Verification Mission’s mandate and supporting survivors of conflict-related and gender-based violence.

The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its support for Colombia’s efforts to broaden peace through dialogue and will continue to work closely with the Colombian authorities, the Verification Mission, and our partners on the Council to achieve a stable and peaceful future for all Colombians.
